correctness.rationale: For two omitted vertices \(x,y\), the complement of \(\{x,y\}\) is 2-dominating exactly when either they are nonadjacent and both have degree at least two, or they are adjacent and both have degree at least three. Since any 2-dominating set of size at most \(n-2\) can be enlarged to size \(n-2\), this proves \(\gamma_2=n-1\) iff \(H=\{d\ge2\}\) is a clique and at most one member of \(H\) has degree at least three. Under \(m=2\), \(|H|\ge\lceil n/2\rceil\), while the clique condition forces \(|H|\le3\), hence \(n\le6\). The cases \(|H|=1,2,3\) then give exactly the listed graphs. A fresh independent exhaustive check through order five reproduced the structural lemma; the universal order bound is analytic.
